residual_risks: Parallel test runs with fork start method: the class-level DatabaseWrapper._connection_pools dict is inherited by forked workers. setup_worker_connection() (base creation.py:377-384) only updates NAME and calls close(); it never calls close_pool(). If the parent recreated the pool after _clone_test_db() (e.g. a system check or feature probe connecting between clone and fork), workers would reuse a pool that has no worker threads and points at the original test DB, with idle sockets shared across processes. Whether the parent reconnects before forking was not confirmed.

The pool is keyed only by alias and built from get_connection_params() at first use. Code that opens a pooled connection before create_test_db() changes NAME (e.g. AppConfig.ready() queries) would keep serving connections to the non-test database, because only _clone_test_db/_destroy_test_db/ensure_timezone close the pool. This is not confirmed for the default runner flow.

Pooled code paths in creation.py (_clone_test_db/_destroy_test_db close_pool), features.django_test_skips pool branch, close_if_health_check_failed pool short-circuit, and NO_DB_ALIAS bypass are reachable only by running the full suite with OPTIONS['pool'] enabled; no such settings/CI config exists in the repo (grep-only check of .github/ and tests/*.py), so they rely on external CI.
No live PostgreSQL available; none of the new tests were executed, so pass/fail conclusions are from reading code and psycopg_pool 3.3.3 source.

Pool + default CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS=False: psycopg_pool hands out idle connections without checking them, so after a DB restart or failover each stale pooled connection fails one request. Without pooling, CONN_MAX_AGE=0 always opened a fresh connection. The new docs section does not tell users to enable CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS with pool.

Fork safety: _connection_pools is a class-level dict, and pools are opened lazily. If a pool is opened in a pre-fork master (e.g. gunicorn --preload with DB access at import or ready time), children inherit idle sockets shared with the parent and lose the pool's worker threads, so the pool cannot grow or reconnect. Not verified against a live server.

No reset callback is configured, so session state set by one borrower (SET search_path/statement_timeout, session advisory locks, temp tables, LISTEN) now leaks to borrowers in other threads. Before, it stayed within one thread's persistent connection.

close_pool() closes a process-wide pool from the setting_changed TIME_ZONE/USE_TZ handler (ensure_timezone) while other threads, such as a LiveServer thread, may hold checked-out connections. Tests only; not exercised.

Parallel test runs with fork: if the parent reopens a pool for an alias after _clone_test_db closed it (e.g. a DB-hitting check in run_checks), forked workers inherit _connection_pools with the parent's test DB kwargs and dead worker threads; setup_worker_connection does not close the pool. Not confirmed that run_checks reconnects on PostgreSQL.

close_pool() and ensure_timezone() (fired by setting_changed for TIME_ZONE/USE_TZ) close the shared per-alias pool while other threads (e.g. a LiveServerTestCase server thread) may be between `self.pool` lookup and `pool.open()/getconn()`. A closed pool cannot be reopened, so those threads would get PoolClosed/OperationalError. close_pool's `del` can also KeyError under concurrent callers.

After a connection is closed inside an atomic block, the error type now depends on whether pooling is on. With pooling, the next query raises django.db.ProgrammingError('Cannot open a new connection in an atomic block.') from the new base ensure_connection guard, because pooled _close sets self.connection = None. Without pooling, the stale connection object stays and psycopg's closed-connection error comes back as InterfaceError/OperationalError. Code that catches InterfaceError to detect dropped connections behaves differently with pooling enabled. For non-pooled backends the guard is unreachable, because base close() keeps self.connection inside atomic blocks.

DatabaseWrapper.ensure_timezone() now closes and discards the alias-wide pool shared by all threads, as a side effect. Its only in-tree caller is the test setting_changed signal, but any external caller now tears down the process pool. close_pool() also goes through the self.pool property, which builds a pool (or raises ImproperlyConfigured when CONN_MAX_AGE != 0) just to close it.
callsite completeness: grep-only. I did not survey third-party subclasses that override ensure_role/ensure_timezone/init_connection_state, so the size of the hook-bypass finding is inferred.

testing_gaps: No pooled-connection test sets OPTIONS['assume_role']; such a test would have exposed the configure-callback re-entry deadlock.

No test checks that a pooled connection gets the configured isolation_level, or that a connection taken from the pool after another borrower switched autocommit off comes back in the state set by settings AUTOCOMMIT.

ImportError branch for psycopg_pool ('Error loading psycopg_pool module') has no test; mock.patch.dict(sys.modules, {'psycopg_pool': None}) with pool=True and asserting ImproperlyConfigured would cover it.

assume_role applied via the pool's configure callback is untested: with pool enabled, a nonexistent role fails inside the pool worker (connection discarded) and surfaces as PoolTimeout after the timeout rather than InvalidParameterValue as test_connect_role asserts for the non-pooled path.
close_if_health_check_failed() pooled early-return has no positive test; the two base health-check tests are merely skipped under pool.
No test combines OPTIONS pool with assume_role (test_connect_role is forced through no_pool_connection), which would have exposed the configure-callback re-entry.
No test covers close() inside atomic() with AUTOCOMMIT=False followed by a query after the block; the new ensure_connection guard is only tested by setting the flags manually.
No test combines OPTIONS['pool'] with OPTIONS['assume_role'] (test_connect_role deliberately uses no_pool_connection), which is how the configure-callback re-entrancy deadlock went unnoticed.
No test checks that a pool created before create_test_db/set_as_test_mirror is discarded so pooled connections reach the test database.
